providers.title: The eigenvalue problems
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). The first Dirichlet eigenvalue and the first positive Neumann eigenvalue are attained; the Neumann eigenspace is finite-dimensional, consists of functions smooth up to the boundary, and contains no nonzero function vanishing on an open set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filonov's gap
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). For a bounded simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary (the proof uses only connectedness), the first positive Neumann eigenvalue is strictly smaller than the first Dirichlet eigenvalue.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Strict hot spots
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). On a bounded simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary, no eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has an interior critical point; its maximum and minimum are attained only on the boundary.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hopf's boundary point lemma
providers.scope: A subharmonic function on a disc, continuously differentiable up to a boundary point where it attains a strict maximum, has positive outward normal derivative there.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Conformal maps smooth up to the boundary
providers.scope: A bounded simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary is the image of the unit disc under a conformal map that extends to a diffeomorphism of the closures with nonvanishing derivative.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A positive boundary weight
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). A smooth positive weight on the circle annihilates the pulled-back boundary values of every first Neumann eigenfunction; these boundary values are nonzero and take both signs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Planar separation
providers.scope: Two paths in the closed unit disc, with interiors in the open disc, joining alternating pairs of points of the circle, intersect.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Connected sign sets
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). The positive and negative sets of a first Neumann eigenfunction are connected, and its boundary values show no four alternating strict signs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiplicity at most two
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). The first positive Neumann eigenvalue of a bounded simply connected planar domain with smooth boundary has multiplicity at most two.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rohleder's variational principle
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). For tangent H^1 vector fields the divergence-curl energy is at least mu times the squared L^2 norm, with equality exactly for gradients of first Neumann eigenfunctions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The curvature identity
providers.scope: For tangent vector fields of class C^2 up to the boundary, the divergence-curl energy equals the Dirichlet energy plus the boundary integral of the curvature times |X|^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Green representation in the disc
providers.scope: The Green integral of an L^2 function on the unit disc is defined and continuous at every point and is the weak solution of the Dirichlet problem with zero boundary values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Green operator of a subcritical potential
providers.scope: For a bounded nonnegative potential q with a Dirichlet inequality of constant d < 1, the Green operator is self-adjoint on L^2(q) with norm at most d.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Boundary kernels
providers.scope: The kernels K and R built from the Poisson kernel and the Green operator are finite off the diagonal, R is symmetric with total integral at most q(D)/(1-d), and K represents the solution of the Dirichlet problem with the potential.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Douglas's identity
providers.scope: The Dirichlet energy of the Poisson extension of a Lipschitz function h on the circle is half the double integral of |h(s)-h(t)|^2/(pi |s-t|^2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The multiplier identity
providers.scope: Assume (SOB) and (ER). For the boundary gradient g of a first Neumann eigenfunction and every real Lipschitz b on the circle, E(bg) is half the double integral of N(s,t)(b(s)-b(t))^2 g(s).g(t).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Matrices with one positive eigenvalue
providers.scope: Having at most one positive eigenvalue is preserved by congruence, by subtracting positive semidefinite matrices, by principal submatrices and by limits; a rank-one matrix minus a positive semidefinite one has it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Conditional negativity
providers.scope: For a bounded nonnegative subcritical potential on the disc and every interior point p, the kernel K(p,s)K(p,t)/N(s,t) on the circle is conditionally negative semidefinite.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Regularized Green kernels
providers.scope: There are bounded continuous kernels C_eps increasing to the Green function of the disc whose finite entrywise-reciprocal matrices have at most one positive eigenvalue.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rank-one updates
providers.scope: If the entrywise reciprocal of a positive symmetric matrix M has at most one positive eigenvalue, so does the entrywise reciprocal of M + c M_iz M_zj for c >= 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A Hilbert-space embedding of the circle
providers.scope: For every interior point p of the disc there is an injective Lipschitz map b from the circle into a separable Hilbert space with |b(s)-b(t)|^2 = K(p,s)K(p,t)/N(s,t).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
